correctness.rationale: Every degree-two flip requires its two neighbors to flip in the opposite phase; propagation forces both chord endpoints and classifies each arc as entirely flipping or stationary. Stationary words are exactly no-singleton-run words with an exceptional admissible length-one case. Their boundary GF gives Fibonacci A and six-periodic D. The four disjoint endpoint phase/arc combinations give the asserted formula; Binet bounds yield uniform golden-ratio entropy and bulk prefactor. Two independent standard-library verifiers replayed: 48 complete graph cases (830112 configurations, n=5..16), plus stationary-word enumeration through length 17 and recurrence checks through 100. All-length proof does not rely on finite tests.

originality.rationale: The claim is a complete two-parameter initial period-two census with endpoint-flip rigidity and uniform/bulk entropy. Relevant general threshold-period theorems, majority convergence results, regularly chorded-ring dynamo literature and neighbouring exact graph-family counts do not imply it on their stated hypotheses. Exact searches and claim-level comparisons were carried out; first-priority claims about inaccessible old articles remain conditional, and no absolute historical uniqueness is asserted.
residual_risks: Complete original Goles–Olivos 1980/1981 texts were not obtained; despite their broad abstract claim, an unexpected graph-specific corollary cannot be fully ruled out.
The literature and table searches are necessarily nonexhaustive; an equivalent formula in unindexed work could exist.

value.rationale: Single-chord insertion is a minimal natural graph perturbation; it creates exponentially many primitive two-cycle states even on odd cycles where the undecorated cycle has none. The exact all-distance formula exposes two-arc boundary interaction and parity effects, and the bulk leading asymptotic shows universality across all chord placements whose two arcs grow. The structural endpoint-flip classification and all-length entropy address mathematically motivated recurrent-state invariants rather than arbitrary sizes or minor numerical improvements.
